posts.title: 4th person Pronouns
posts.description: I love English, it's such a complicated language. So many different rules, and exceptions to the rules, and then exceptions to the exceptions to the rules. It's just so much fun. I've learned a couple of other languages like Spanish, and Korean, and while each is unique in their own way, nothing really beats the fluidity and creativity of English. I watched a video online, and they proposed that the word "Chat" might be the worlds first ever usage of a 4th person pronoun. Kids in the newer generations use it all the time, imitating live stream influencers. My favorite is the expression, "Chat, is this even real?" in completely real world, not being recorded or streamed, language. What a time to be alive to see how language and culture is being influenced! For me, I always love to see how things change. So many people are against it, and I don't understand. posts.title: AI in Business
posts.description: After working with so many businesses on AI, I've come to the conclusion that I don't know how most small businesses stay in business. AI isn't the problem, I want to start with that. AI is just the example that led me down this rabbit hole. I've read in a couple of places (and I don't know how true it is, but in my anecdotal experience, it's fairly accurate for me) that most business are failing to use AI, or the AI isn't actually improving the business or reducing costs. I didn't get it at first, but after talking to a lot of business owners, and seeing their experiences, I kinda understand why. Most companies before AI, would go out to the internet to find whatever software they needed. If you're a dentist, you go find one of the 3 main dental softwares, if you're an engineer, you find whatever version of AutoCad most suites your type of engineer, if you're a law firm, you find the law firm software you want to use. posts.title: Other people are not me
posts.description: Today, I'm really struggling not to judge people by the standards I set for myself. It sounds like I'm being petty and conceited, but let me explain. I had a customer call, and for about an hour, I tried to walk them through installing software on their computer. It was very frustrating. It wasn't a particularly difficult install. It took 15 minutes just to explain what I meant by "web browser" when I said, "Open your web browser and go to [redacted] website". My gut reaction to this interaction was, "this person is a moron". I don't want to go on a tangent on why I should be able to say what I want, even if it's rude or discriminatory, as long as it's true, so I won't comment on my use of the word "moron". All that said, while going through the exhausting exercise of patience set before me, I started thinking about this person and wondering why they were so bad at technology.
